subject: human liver
title: Surgeons Can Remove Two-Thirds of Your Liver. It Grows Back

scenes.text: Doctors can cut away most of one organ in your body. It grows back.
A healthy liver can lose up to two-thirds of itself and still recover.
Living donors give up to sixty percent of theirs to save someone else.
In about six weeks, both pieces grow into full-sized, working livers.
The cells that are left start dividing again, within days.
One liver goes in. Two come out. No other organ in you can do that.

description:
A healthy liver can lose up to two-thirds of its volume and regrow, according to Cleveland Clinic. Living donors can give up to 60% of theirs.
Michigan Medicine says that in about six weeks the donated part grows into a normal-sized liver in the recipient while the donor's liver regrows too.
Which organ would you most like to be able to regrow?
first_comment: A damaged liver can only lose about a third, so this works best on a healthy one. What other body fact should we cover?
